reason: The cited evidence (E1-E3) from a single study on a different alloy system (TiZrHfCuNi) demonstrates an irreversible glass-to-glass transition with enhanced ordering and thermal stability upon sub-Tg annealing. However, the hypothesis makes specific claims about phosphorus-containing high-entropy alloys, for which no direct evidence is provided. The extrapolation from the cited system to the proposed CrMnFeCoNiP alloy is a significant gap, leaving the key premises unsupported for the target material.
premises: Sub-Tg annealing of a P-containing high-entropy amorphous alloy can induce an irreversible glass-to-glass transition.
This transition enhances short- and medium-range atomic ordering.
The enhanced ordering reduces internal free volume and nucleation sites.
The structural changes kinetically stabilize the amorphous phase, increasing thermal stability.
The treatment improves glass-forming ability, as indicated by a broader supercooled liquid region.
